reason: I'd try it in my hour after the kids are down, a session built from my own sentence is a nicer idea than Calm's library. But I paid Calm once and quit in a month, and I won't pay again until I know where my mental-state notes go.
objection: I'm typing how I feel into an AI and I have no idea who reads it or what it's used for.
would_change_my_mind: A plain privacy page that says my words are not stored or used for training, and a delete-everything button.

v1.why: Opens on someone else's chat and a coin counter; feels like a game, not something private.

v2.why: Cleaner and my own conversation, but nothing tells me what happens to what I said.

v3.why: Private journal and progress in words feel like it is for me; I'd keep the free tier going.

reason: Free to try, so sure, I'll make one or two. I've never paid for one of these and I know I'll drop it the way I drop my journal.
objection: Another subscription I'd forget to use while it bills me every month.

v1.why: Daily check-in sheet feels like homework I'll fail at.

v2.why: Nice welcome, but it'll fall off by week two like everything else.

v3.why: The journal is appealing but I already don't keep a journal; it'd lapse.

reason: I'm awake scrolling most weeknights anyway, and a sleep session made for 'my mind won't switch off' beats picking the same rain track again. Ten dollars is nothing to me if it actually gets me to sleep, so I'd pay once the free limit bites.
objection: I don't want it quizzing me every morning about how I slept; I want to press play and drift off.

v1.why: The daily check-in pop-up after sign-in is exactly the nagging I don't want.

v2.why: Three skippable questions once, then tabs and a play button; that I'd use at bedtime.

v3.why: Fine too, but more journal and check-in stuff than I need; I'd ignore those parts.

reason: At bedtime I just tap the sleep sounds I already have; I'm not opening a browser and typing a sentence when I'm wrecked. Maybe when the phone app is out.
objection: I already have free apps and YouTube that do this with one tap.
would_change_my_mind: A real phone app with a one-tap 'sleep' button and no typing.

v1.why: Hamburger menu, coins and a check-in before I can sleep; no.

v2.why: Simpler, but still more steps than my free sleep app.

v3.why: Journal and reports are nice ideas I won't use at 11pm.

reason: I'd try a couple between therapy sessions in my evening hour, the idea of a session built around exactly what I'm feeling is good. I'm not paying or pouring real stuff into it until I know what's kept about my mental state.
objection: What happens to what I tell it about how I'm doing, and could it say something unhelpful to someone in a bad place?
would_change_my_mind: Clear data policy plus something showing a clinician or therapist had a hand in how it talks.

v1.why: Percentages and red arrows on my wellbeing feel like being graded.

v2.why: Better, but still scores my progress, which my therapist would never do.

v3.why: Words not numbers, a Why? on changes and a private journal fit how I already work on myself.

reason: I'd try it because hooking it to my sleep tracker is interesting. But money's tight with the kids and I already know I'd stop opening it after a few weeks.
objection: Another ten a month I'll forget to use.
would_change_my_mind: If it actually moved my sleep score over a couple of weeks on the free tier, I'd think about the yearly plan.

v1.why: Wellness percentages that are clearly not from my data put me off.

v2.why: Okay, but nothing connects to the tracker I actually check.

v3.why: Asks which wearable I use and leaves it off till I choose; that's respectful, I'd keep the free tier.

reason: An AI writing and voicing my meditation is exactly what I don't want near my head. I'll stick with real teachers and my sleep tracker.
objection: AI-made meditation sounds generic at best and a bit creepy at worst.
would_change_my_mind: Hearing a full sample that sounds human and having a friend I trust swear by it.

v1.why: 'Based on the diagnosis' from an AI, and coins; worst of both.

v2.why: Still AI writing my mental-health audio.

v3.why: The Why? explanations help a little, but I wouldn't use it.

reason: I'll try it, it's free and making my own session is more interesting than Headspace's library. But I paid for Headspace and quit after a month, so I'll ride the free tier and see if I'm still opening it in week three.
objection: I don't want an app asking me questions every day; that's why I quit the last one.
would_change_my_mind: Still using it daily after a month on free; then $100 a year is an easy yes.

v1.why: Daily check-in sheet the moment I sign in; out.

v2.why: Questions once, skippable, then just make and play; I'd keep it a while.

v3.why: Journal, check-ins and two-week reports start to feel like the questioning I avoid.

reason: I'd try a few on my commute since I'm in headphones anyway. A few free sessions a day is more than I'd ever use, so I can't see why I'd pay.
objection: Another subscription I'd forget about; the free tier already covers me.

v1.why: Feels cluttered and the coins make me think it'll nickel-and-dime me.

v2.why: Easy tabs, quick to make one on the train; free tier is plenty.

v3.why: Same as v2 for me; I'd skip the journal.

reason: My commute already has podcasts and free meditations from real people. I don't trust AI-generated stuff for my head, so I wouldn't bother signing up.
objection: I already have free apps and YouTube for this, made by humans.
would_change_my_mind: Listening to a sample without signing up and it not sounding like AI.

v1.why: 'Aurelia AI can make mistakes' next to mental health advice; no thanks.

v3.why: Least pushy of the three, but I'd still not use it.
